context.body: Selected for the reader trail because “Accusations move from Pilate to Herod and back” preserves a distinct parallel witness source unit within sentencing.
context.label: Narrative or literary frame

observations.body: Accusation before Pilate moves to Herod, mockery, return, repeated findings, a proposed punishment, and final delivery.
observations.label: Accusations move from Pilate to Herod and back: textual observation

observations.body: The accusations concern nation, tribute, and kingship; Pilate and Herod are repeatedly said not to find a capital charge.
observations.label: Accusations move from Pilate to Herod and back: action, promise, or consequence

observations.body: Chief priests, crowds, Pilate, Herod, soldiers, and Barabbas act while Jesus’ answers remain sparse.
observations.label: Relationships named in Luke 23:1–25

payload.posture: Read Luke 23:1–25 as its own sentencing and mockery crucifixion setting before carrying its language into another source.
payload.tension: Repeated official findings do not determine the outcome; Luke says the voices prevail.
payload.title: Accusations move from Pilate to Herod and back
